task: It's good that you asked. We do have a job for you. Planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system is believed to be involved in a conflict with one of the gaalian planets. You can't even imagine - a couple of gaals show up on <ToPlanet>; then they arrest everybody on the planet for possession and consumption of narcotic drugs! They should be arrested for not using drugs! Do you know what kind of economic growth the pelengs would see if lots of gaals started buying their drugs? I'm sorry, I digress. Anyway, we need a chief sorter at the planet's orbiting military sorting customs station. If you want to participate in this glorious mission on behalf of peleng race, and in so doing earn at least <Money> credits, then take this mission quickly. Remember the military actions begin in <Day> days!
success:
Well, it seems rangers really can do everything…
Yes, secretary. Thank you, put it right here... (Crunch, crunch crunch...) Ah, it's so good! As always, you've done everything splendidly. Planets <FromPlanet> and <ToPlanet> convey their gratitude to you.  Here's your <Money> cr. Goodbye.
loc.1.0:
You returned to the planet's orbit. The military base was a gigantic iron box, about the size of an entire city block, suspended in orbit. There was something like rusty jaws with iron teeth on the front, and you flew into it through these.
You touched down on the landing pad in one of the hangars. It was humid and a slight chill found its way through holes in your threadbare ranger suit. You were met by a happy-looking peleng wearing a greasy and grimy uniform. 
"Ah, it's the great sorter <Ranger>!" exclaimed the peleng with a wink. "I've been tasked with bringing you up to date. My name is Borzuhan."
"I'm very curious. What does this job entail?"
"For shipping freight and soldiers, we use a cross between a regular transport ship and a gravitrain. Your task is to sort <clr>thirty<clrEnd> of these trains. Each train has between two and ten railcars. There are a total of <clr>four tracks<clrEnd> in the railroad yard. Each track can hold <clr>twenty cars<clrEnd>. If all twenty railcars are put together into a single train on any of the tracks, the built-in engines will immediately start moving it. There also will be <clr>big locotractors<clrEnd> at your disposal, in addition to the ordinary ones. Each of them can move any number of railcars all at once. But there is a problem - <clr>If more than twenty railcars are put on one track <clrEnd>, there won’t be enough power on the line for them to move, and <clr>the track will close automatically <clrEnd>.
 There are <clr>four kinds of railcars: personnel cars, weaponry cars, fuel cars, and machinery cars<clrEnd>. You cannot connect cars with different contents, because it makes it very difficult for us to later redirect them where they need to go. For each such infraction or for blocking the tracks, we will write you up and fine you 50 credits. <clr>If you get more than three write-ups, we'll have to let you go.<clrEnd> Well, will you take the job? Or do you have any questions?"
loc.1.1:
The peleng sighed.
"Wow, <Ranger>. This is like two plus two. We're going to send you trains, and you sort them on the tracks. As soon as you have 20 cars on a track, it will be cleared automatically and you can carry on working. If there is more than twenty cars, the track will be closed, and you won’t be able to work with it anymore. We'll have to write you up for blocking the tracks. Is there something else you don't understand? Or are you ready to do this now?
loc.1.2: "The big locotractors will help you clear the cars from a track," explained the peleng. "We'll send you locotractors from time to time instead of the regular train. Just dispatch the locotractor to the desired track, and all the cars will be moved out. You also have some backup locotractors. Each of them can clear just a few cars from a track. You can use them whenever you want. "Well, do you have any more questions? Or are you ready to get to work?"
loc.1.3: "Isn't that difficult to understand? You can't connect cars that contain different things. If you do connect cars that contain different things, we'll write you up and fine you. Four write-ups and you're fired. The contents of the last car determine the contents of the train. In other words, if you connect five personnel cars to five weaponry cars, we'll write you up and the train will be considered a "personnel train". Is everything clear now? Will you take the job?"
loc.2.0: From one of the numerous pockets on your threadbare ranger suit, you fish out a tin of your favorite Machpella Dark and make yourself more comfortable on the rough planks of a box. Forgetting yourself, you, out of habit, tried to recline backward, this model of chair lacked a back. As a result, you lost your balance and crashed to the ground. You suddenly recalled an unforgettable story about how the phrase "Sit back and relax" had to be removed from the installation menus for the Macrohard Doors operating system, because so many maloqs complained about constantly falling off their much-praised stools. Having regained your composure, you opened your beer and started waiting.
loc.2.1: Waiting for the train was obviously good for your condition. You indulged in nostalgic thoughts about your past heroic deeds, clever ambushes, and long patrols. You began to wait for the train, like a predator waits for his victim, concealing himself deftly in tall grass. Actually, hiding was out of the question; after all, the walls of your cabin were rather like a sieve.
loc.2.2: You got bored, took out a laptop, and turned it on. It greeted you with beautiful text and jingled a pleasant melody. You put on your headphones, started playing your favorite cyberpunk band – Blin 182 – and launched your favorite game: Sirtet. The point of the game was to take to break down groups of small squares into their constituent parts as quickly and skillfully as possible. The game sure makes the time fly by!
loc.2.3:
A boy ran into the cabin and said with a voice that was imploring, yet contemptuous and, at the same time, jolly ("He must have worked long and hard to produce this kind of sound", you thought): 
"Hey, Mister. Give me a cigarette!"
"I don't smoke!" you answer proudly. 
"Aha! "On planet <ToPlanet>, non-smoking is prohibited by law! It's punishable by two months in prison and partial confiscation of your property!" said the peleng triumphantly. "But if you give me a credit, I won’t tell anyone anything..." His tone changed to patronizing and sly. 
You dragged the young extortioner out of your cabin by his collar and sent him to where he ought to be – the tower.
loc.2.4:
You noticed a young peleng in military uniform marching around the cabin. You called him over and asked,
"What are you doing here, going back and forth?"
"Patrolling!" answered the peleng with a sharp salute.
"Very well, patrol away…" you replied absentmindedly.
"He's probably guarding the cabin so nobody burglarizes it," you decide and go back to your workstation.
loc.2.5:
Life on the tracks was hectic. Switchmen, loaders, and repairmen ran every which way. Maybe if it wasn’t so corny, you would compare it with ant hill that had been attacked by a shovel-wielding kid. Here and there, metal speakers broadcasted a woman’s voice, which was accompanied by an awful echo and incredible distortion. The voice communicated something to the train engineers. They responded in like manner, except with men's voices. You only managed to understand one phrase in all your time in the train yard: "Numbering begins from the rear end of the train," though you couldn't entirely grasp what this meant. 
You began to think deeply - where was this mysterious rear end? Maybe it was at the very end of the train - the last car; but, on the other hand, maybe the rear end was the very first in the rear. And where exactly does the rear begin anyway? And where does part that's "not the rear" end? You had more questions, but your curious ranger mind couldn't find any logical answer.
loc.2.6: A peleng worker caught your attention. He was carrying something under his upper right arm. It vaguely resembled a cross-tie that weighed no more than five kilograms. He held an open bottle of beer in every other hand. Every third step, he squatted, gasped deeply, took and swig from one of the bottles, and indistinctly murmured something like, "Oooff. I am so tired!..." Then he mopped up some sweat with the back of the hand.
loc.4.0: The head of the peleng errand boy popped into a crack in the door and declared: "A train with [p14] <clr>weaponry cars<clrEnd> is coming." You placed your hands on the levers. The handles feel more like rough sandpaper or a fine grater than ordinary iron balls.
loc.4.1: The noise set in almost imperceptibly. It seems it was quiet just a moment ago, but now you had to cover your ears it was so loud. With wild groans and clattering, the train careened right toward you, threatening to jump off the tracks. Somewhere deep in the wide expanse of your ranger heart, there appeared a desire to get to know the station's designer. The boy tried to shout something, but it looked more like a mime show. It was a good thing that you had learned how to read lips in your day! You understood what he said perfectly: "A train with [p14] <clr>weapon cars<clrEnd> is coming."
loc.4.2: You glanced out the window and watched the shiny, slowly-approaching lunkers. It was a train of [p14] <clr>personnel cars<clrEnd>. The fact that it moved slowly and noiselessly gave the impression that it wanted to sneak up undetected and surreptitiously raze your distressed cabin.
loc.4.3:
You heard a soft buzz and invited the errand boy in. When he came in, you asked,
"Who's coming over there?"
"A king..."
"What king?"
"King? I don't know any king!"
"Okay, what's that train over there?" 
"A train with [p14] <clr>personnel cars<clrEnd>.
loc.4.4: The boy ran to you, caught his breath, and reported, "A train with [p14] <clr>fuel cars<clrEnd> is coming."
loc.4.5: The first thing you sensed was the smell. You didn't know what kind of smell it was, but you could detect ammonia and acetylene in bouquet of aromas. It was impossible not to recognize the train – the half-melted, filthy canisters resembled a bunch of gigantic sausages. The boy who came into the cabin gasped for air and declared, "This (cough) train has (cough, cough) [p14] <clr>fuel cars<clrEnd>."
loc.4.6: The approaching train reminded you of your childhood. You had always wanted a toy train like that, equipped with beautiful examples of military technology. With his shout of "A train with [p14] <clr>machinery cars<clrEnd> is arriving," your assistant brought you back from your daydreaming.
loc.4.7: You glanced out the window and saw a rapidly approaching plasma tank. The scene would have been much scarier if the peleng loaders hadn't contrived to secretly steal a cannon and a part of the track. The tank stood on the platform for transport cars. The peleng shouted from the tower, "A train with [p14] <clr>machinery cars<clrEnd> is coming!"
loc.6.0: "This isn't a job for a real ranger!" you shouted and started toward your ship. "So what if I don't make some money on a couple of cannons or luxury freight? I'll have a lot less stress in my life as a result!"
loc.10.0:
You watched the screen to the right of the levers. Through the dusty, greasy glass, you can read:

"At your disposal, you have:
[p27] Argberger locotractors
[p28] Tshaipyu locotractors
[p29] Tosharak locotractors
[p30] Sanleo locotractors
[p31] Isou locotractors

Locotractor capacity:
<clr>Argberger<clrEnd> - 1 car
<clr>Tshaipyu<clrEnd> - 2 cars
<clr>Tosharak<clrEnd> - 3 cars
<clr>Sanleo<clrEnd> - 4 cars
<clr>Isou<clrEnd> - 5 cars"
loc.11.0: The Argberger locotractor wasn't really like a locotractor. It was more like a regular passenger railcar. The errand peleng said that it was regular railcar, but with a more powerful standalone engine. You put your hand over the levers and began thinking about where to send this happiness.
loc.11.1: Something covered in soot came riding out from a lateral line. The construction resembled an ancient clothes iron. Steam and some sort of gas bellowed out of several holes on the bottom. The lunker came up to a fork in the track, stopped, and waited.
loc.11.2: The Tosharak resembled some torpedo with tubes protruding from each side. There wasn't a single tiny window on its smooth, shiny surface. It gave the impression that the entire thing was made of steel. You put your hand over the levers and began thinking about where to send this happiness.
loc.11.3: The Sanleo locotractor looked like an iron chest with an engine. It had seen better days: on each side there were sheets of iron falling from the sideboards in places, exposing to view the sophisticated machinery underneath. You began to think about which track to send this unit to.
loc.11.4: If didn't already know that the Isou was a locotractor, you probably would have thought it was some endurance racecar. Sheer power seemed to emanate from the machine. The only thing missing was some threatening spikes or a couple of circular saws mounted on the hood.
loc.12.0:
"Well, it’s up to you," answered the peleng without any well-wishing in his voice.
He led you to the engine house, where your spaceship was located. Sitting in the pilot's seat, you thought, "I think it's be easier to beat the dominators than to sort railcars."
loc.12.1:
Borzuhan knocked on the cabin door. He looked tired and sad.
"You gave us a lot of trouble. We have to unblock the trains in the few hours remaining before the start of the workday." 
You drop your head. The lyakusha led you silently to the engine house, where your spaceship was located. Sitting in the pilot's seat, you thought, "I think it's be easier to beat the dominators than to sort railcars."
loc.12.2:
A smiling Borzuhan knocked on the cabin door. You stepped outside, and he shook your hand with all four of his.
"I've never seen such clever humanoid!"
You blushed a little and said,
"I didn’t expect to hear words like that coming from a peleng!"
Instead of responding, the lyakusha gave you a thick wad of galacredits, which you stuffed into your wallet, and led you to your ship. Sitting in the pilot's seat, you thought, "I think it's be easier to beat the dominators than to sort railcars."
loc.13.0:
"Okay, agreed then! By the way, since you're not a commanding officer, there won't be any fines!" the peleng called out with a wink. 
Apparently, the workday at the base had ended. The main light was switched off, leaving only small lamps, which were apparently never switched off, under the ceiling to lighten the room. Most of the pelengs left their places. Only those who were in on Borzuhan’s plan remained. 
After leading you to your cabin, he disappeared somewhere without a trace.

loc.17.0:
"Stop!!!" you shouted, as you ran out of the cabin as if the place was on fire. "All the tracks are closed!" 
The train stopped. Borzuhan, dark as a thundercloud, appeared out of nowhere. 
"You can't trust these rangers with anything! You can't do anything but push a button! Not only did you fail your mission, but you've clogged up the station! Or maybe you're a saboteur?
As you were taken to your ship, he was still muttering something unintelligible about his problems, some sort of furry pet, and something else. Soon, you were standing in complete solitude near your spaceship.
jump.2.text: Go to hell. I'm not going to get involved in this stupidity!
jump.3.desc:
"Wonderful!" said peleng, leading you somewhere farther inside. "We have a little secret. The railcars that aren't attached to a train - the ones that stay on the tracks - can be written off as non-functional. In fact, that's what we usually do, and then they can be used for contraband. So we'll pay you 10 credits for every car that stays on the tracks," he said and winked cheerfully. "Oh yes, there's one more thing. We have five different kinds of mini-locotractors. You can use them whenever you want. The capacity of each of them is written on the panel to the right of the levers."
After getting through all the terminals, custom examinations, pat-downs, and other such procedures, you at last arrived at your workstation. You expected to see a large, computerized room with all sorts of holographic matrices, mental interfaces, and similar achievements of science and technology. Instead, your room more closely resembled a village outhouse that had been hastily finished with old gray planks. The space inside the cabin was at most one and half square meters. Half of the space was occupied by a rusty control panel with four levers that were labeled as follows: "To the first track", "To the second track", and so on.  A lazy young peleng who runs errands serves as the reporting system for arriving trains. You immediately sent him to the short lookout tower. You spent the first fifteen minutes of your work time looking for something that could be used as a chair. So instead of the comfy, spinning armchair that you had dreamed about, all you found was a dusty crate for beer bottles. You put it near the control panel right away.
This whole nightmare of an office was right in the middle of the tracks and a switch thrown too late would mean certain death under a train.
"Well, let’s get to work!" you think to yourself.
jump.5.desc: The boy ran into your cabin and shouted, "There's a locotractor coming!" though this was quite evident even without him. A huge, awful machine raced along the rails. Covered with soot, it had the power of a furious gobsaurus and made sounds which could only be produced by an inebriated brass band. This monstrosity must be dispatch to some track soon, or it will just run off the track and smash the cabin to hell.
jump.6.text: Put it on the first track
jump.6.desc: Your predecessor evidently did not like the first track. The lever was so rusty that the switch could only be moved by bringing all your strength to bear.
jump.7.text: Put it on the second track
jump.7.desc: It seems that the lever is conspiring with the train. While the lever resists your efforts, the train rushes straight toward your cabin without slowing. After a long, exhausting struggle, you won the arm wrestling match and threw over the switch.
jump.8.text: Put it on the third track
jump.8.desc: With great effort, you moved the lever for the third track. It wasn't going to give up so easily and scratched you deep enough to draw blood. You managed to throw the switch and, with a soft clang, the train headed for the third track.
jump.9.text: Put it on the fourth track
jump.9.desc: You pushed the lever with all your might, and it obediently surrendered.

jump.22.desc: The train assembled on the first track started its journey out into the big world and left the track itself free of unnecessary railcars.
jump.23.desc: There was a stir on the second track, and soon the assembled train had cleared the track.
jump.24.desc: There was a stir on the third track, and soon the assembled train had cleared the track.
jump.25.desc: "The Lyanchak-Peykhats train is leaving on the fourth track! Be careful!" commanded an iron voice. The transport slowly departed and then rushed to its destination.
jump.26.desc: A light blinked unexpectedly, and you heard the groan of heavy metal panels. It seems <clr>the first track<clrEnd> can't withstand this many cars.

jump.30.desc:
You were prepared for the next train when the boy reported that everything had been sorted. You stretched and got up from your improvised chair. When Borzuhan came in, he wasn’t pleased with your work,
"I never seen such an incompetent sorter! I can’t believe it! Did you accidentally forget about the cars we wanted to write-off?! And what about the fines? In short, you owe us {-(([p2]+[p5]+[p8]+[p11])*10-([p16]*50))} cr. But since you did in fact accomplish your mission, fly away before we change our minds about letting you go..."
But before you could move, some idea popped into Borzuhan's head. He put upper right hand on your shoulder and pulled you aside. In smooth voice, he said, 
"At the station here, we've got 20 written-off trains. We'll certainly find a good use for them. But first, we need them to be sorted as well. Would you like to do some freelance work? I have to warn you - we had to block the fourth track with the defective cars, so it's closed. And there aren't any new mini-locotractors in sight. Use the ones that are left. I'll pay you <clr>3000<clrEnd> cr. for your work, agreed?

param.15.crit:
You even didn’t notice as Borzuhan entered the cabin. He said,
"Our generals are having real difficulty properly dispatching the trains with their varied contents. We have to dismiss you because of the excessive number of complaints that have been lodged against you and the exorbitant fines you've incurred."
As you were taken to your ship, he was still muttering something unintelligible about his problems, some sort of furry pet, and something else. Soon, you were standing in solitude near your starship.
